description: The entry page and router. It accepts a run id, a capture id, a pull request number or a test id. Find narrows the capture tables, the pull request lookup opens the Pull requests dashboard, the test id lookup opens Trends, and the last table lists every E2E run with its capture verdict, so a run with no capture cannot hide.

panels.title: Start here
panels.description: How to read this page: the run ID format, the links, and the time range.

options.content:
### Start here

This page is a router. It accepts a run id or a capture id in **Find**, a pull request from **Pull request lookup**, a test id from **Test id lookup**, or nothing.

**Find** narrows the cards and the three capture tables, newest first. Type a run id such as `41310072671`, or part of a capture id such as `vmaas-pr123`, then click a row to open that capture.

**Pull request lookup** lists one row per pull request the exporter stored in the last $days days. Click the PR number to open that pull request, already selected, in the Pull requests dashboard.

**Test id lookup** lists one row per test the daily JUnit rollup recorded in the last 7 days, with its runs and failures over that window. Click a test id to open that test, already selected, in the Trends dashboard.

**Four words.** A **span** is one timed step inside a test. A **trace** is all the steps of one operation. A **capture** is one CI run with recording on, and its id is the run id in the tables below. A **cohort** is a set of captures that differ only in what you want to compare.

| To answer | Open |
| --- | --- |
| Which runs exist, and which failed | this page |
| Which runs arrived with no capture | this page, the last table |
| What happened inside one run | [**CI Observe — Capture**](/d/ci-observe-runs/ci-observe-e28094-run-investigation) (click a run id) |
| Where the run's minutes went, step by step | the same page, **CI evidence** row (GitHub jobs, steps, JUnit) |
| What the cluster did during a run | the same page, **Environment** row (pods, CPU, memory) |
| How a change moved from open to merge | [**CI Observe — Pull requests**](/d/ci-observe-pull-requests/ci-observe-pull-requests) |
| Is this test flaky, slower, or newly broken | [**CI Observe — Trends**](/d/ci-observe-trends/ci-observe-trends) |
| Did two runs get slower | [**CI Observe — Trends**, Compare section](/d/ci-observe-trends/ci-observe-e28094-trends) |

**Reading a run ID**: `vmaas-main-41310072671-a1` means suite `vmaas`, branch `main` (a pull request shows `pr123`), GitHub workflow run `41310072671`, and attempt `a1` (the first attempt).

**Runs with no capture.** The last table lists one row per E2E run the workflow exporter recorded in the last $days days, joined to Tempo's capture ids by GitHub run id. Its **Capture** column is the verdict: **capture** means at least one capture id names the run; **not collected** means GitHub has the run and no telemetry arrived; **unknown** means the page could not tell, for a data reason (Tempo was unreachable, a capture lookup chunk was capped, the run is newer than the last lookup, or the run is older than Tempo's 30-day retention). **unknown** is never a claim that a capture is missing: the panel description lists what must be true before it says not collected. **not collected** is a statement about the recording, not about the result, so read the result from the Result column and the logs from GitHub, which keeps them for 7 days.

**Missing session span** means the run's summary span never arrived. The tests may still have passed; the table lists what did arrive. A run that is completely absent never sent any telemetry.

**Time range**: keep the default 7 days. A narrow range can hide a long run. If a run you expect is missing, widen the range up to the 7-day maximum before concluding it never ran. The pull request lookup and the run table ignore the time range and read $days days; the test lookup always reads 7 days, the age at which GitHub deletes a run's artifact.

panels.title: Pull request lookup, one pull request per row, last $days days (workflow exporter)
panels.description: One row per merged or closed pull request the exporter's backfill stored in the last $days days, newest first. The unit is one pull request and its axis is its life, opened to merge or close. The PR cell opens that pull request in the Pull requests dashboard, preselected by number and repository; the GitHub cell opens it on github.com. Only merged and closed pull requests are stored.

defaults.noValue: No pull requests stored for this window

value.title: Open this pull request in the Pull requests dashboard

panels.title: Test id lookup, one test per row, last 7 days (workflow exporter)
panels.description: One row per test the daily JUnit rollup recorded in the last 7 days, with its runs and failures summed over those days. The unit is one test across all its runs and its axis is the 7-day window. The test id cell opens that test in the Trends dashboard, preselected. The sums come from the endpoint, over every rollup row of the window, so they are not cut short by the response row cap. The window is fixed at 7 days because the rollup is built from run artifacts, and GitHub deletes an artifact after 7 days.

defaults.noValue: No per-test rollup rows for the last 7 days

value.title: Open this test in the Trends dashboard

panels.title: Runs with a session span
panels.description: Test runs whose pytest session span arrived in the selected time range. Captures missing their session span are counted separately to the right.

targets.query: { name = "test run" && (status = ok || status = error) && resource."osac.ci.capture_id" =~ ".*${find:regex}.*" }

panels.title: Failed runs
panels.description: Runs whose pytest session ended with an error: at least one test failed. This counts failed runs, not failed tests - see Recent failed tests for the individual failures.

panels.title: Missing session span
panels.description: Captures that recorded test spans but whose session span never arrived (partial telemetry). Their outcome is unknown - not passed. A capture counts as missing when none of its test spans carry the session trace name, so the session span never reached the backend. Listed in the table below.

panels.title: Recent failed tests
panels.description: Failed pytest test spans, newest first. A failed test fails its run, but one failed run can hold several failed tests. A capture can appear more than once when multiple tests failed. Click the run ID to investigate; the menu also offers run comparison.

defaults.noValue: No failed tests in this time range

targets.query: { resource.service.name = "tests" && .pytest.span_type = "test" && name !~ ".*::(setup|call|teardown)" && status = error && resource."osac.ci.capture_id" =~ ".*${find:regex}.*" && ( resource."osac.ci.suite" =~ ".+" || name =~ ".*" ) && ( resource."osac.ci.pr" =~ ".+" || name =~ ".*" ) }

panels.title: Captures with test spans but no session span
panels.description: Runs that sent test spans but no session span. Their status is unknown here: not passed and not failed. The tests may still have succeeded; open one to see what arrived. A run missing from both tables sent no telemetry at all.

defaults.noValue: None: every capture with test spans also has a session span

panels.title: Recent test runs
panels.description: One row per run whose session span arrived, newest first: status and duration come straight from that session span. Captures with test spans but no session span (outcome unknown) are listed in the table above. Click a run ID to investigate; the menu also offers run comparison. GitHub's job conclusion stays authoritative.

defaults.noValue: No test runs found in this time range

targets.query: { name = "test run" && (status = ok || status = error) && resource."osac.ci.capture_id" =~ ".*${find:regex}.*" && ( resource."osac.ci.suite" =~ ".+" || name =~ ".*" ) && ( resource."osac.ci.pr" =~ ".+" || name =~ ".*" ) }

panels.title: Recent E2E runs and their capture, all jobs, last $days days (workflow exporter + Tempo)
panels.description: One row per E2E run the workflow exporter recorded in the last $days days, newest first, joined to Tempo's capture ids on the GitHub run id. Capture says whether a capture arrived: capture (at least one capture id names this run), not collected (GitHub has the run and no telemetry arrived), or unknown (the page could not tell, because Tempo was unreachable, a capture lookup chunk was capped, the run is newer than the last lookup, or the run is older than Tempo's 30-day retention). Clicking the verdict opens the run on GitHub, which is where a not collected run still has its logs for 7 days. The capture tables above follow the page time range; this table follows $days.

defaults.noValue: No E2E runs recorded in the last $days days

value.title: Open this run: its capture when one exists, this page narrowed to it when none does
Open this run on GitHub, where a run with no capture keeps its logs for 7 days

list.name: find
list.label: Find by run id or capture id
list.description: Type a run id (41310072671) or part of a capture id (vmaas-pr123). The cards and the three capture tables narrow to matching runs; the lookup tables and the all-runs table read the workflow exporter and are not narrowed. Empty shows every run in the time range.

list.name: days
list.label: Lookup and run window (days)
list.description: How many days the pull request lookup and the Recent E2E runs table read. It does not affect the capture tables, which follow the dashboard time range, or the test lookup, which always reads 7 days.
